references.text: This verse gives the same number for the tribe of Judah (74,600) as was counted in the first census in Numbers 1.
The second census of the tribe of Judah shows the change in numbers during the wilderness journey (76,500).
Jacob's blessing over Judah foretold the tribe's greatness and leadership, which is reflected in Judah being the largest tribe.
The tribe of Judah under Nahshon's leadership broke camp first when the Israelites left Sinai, confirming their position described in chapter 2.
Nahshon, the leader of Judah mentioned in Numbers 2:3, is an ancestor of Jesus Christ in Matthew's genealogy.
